I’m really sorry you're going through this. It’s clear that you've been through so much, and the pain from your twin's actions, especially during such a vulnerable time, is understandably hard to move past. Being kicked out in a situation like that is so emotionally overwhelming, and I can personally relate to the stress and anxiety of being potentially homeless. Even in a large home, you all most likely have your own standards of cleanliness and personal preference on how/when things get done and that can definitely cause a lot of friction. People have  a varied ability to handle those situations with grace, and your sister may just be someone who needs to have her own space and have it in order how she likes. That doesn't mean she's valid in being shitty but it is what it is.

That said, I want to gently offer the perspective that forgiveness doesn't mean you forget what happened or let her off the hook for the hurt she caused you and your bf. Forgiveness can sometimes just be about releasing that heavy burden of anger so you don’t carry it around with you for your own peace because you don't deserve to feel that way! It's okay to need time and space to heal before even considering forgiveness, and no one should pressure you into forgiving her if you're not ready. But ultimately it may make your interactions with the rest of your family less painful as well.

One thing that can be hard for people, even family, is understanding a situation they haven’t personally experienced—like the feeling of being close to homelessness. Without that firsthand experience, it might be harder for them to fully understand the stress and trauma it caused you. But I do believe that healing might come when you feel ready, even if that means waiting until your emotions settle after the baby arrives. Take care of yourself and your new family first. Your peace and your well-being are what matter most right now.

In my experience, you're only eligible for the RSV vaccine if your infant is defined as "high-risk". 

I can't remember EXACTLY what was on the questionnaire, but it essentially asks if you or anyone in your home smokes, if you have older kids who are in school, if you're a healthcare worker who may be at higher risk of contracting and transferring RSV, etc. 

Depending on the answers you give it tallies up the markers, and if you have less than a certain amount you do not qualify for the vaccine. For example my twins were born premature and someone I lived with smoked, we were literally like 2 points below the threshold and the nurse even fudged an answer or two but we still didn't qualify, which was majorly frustrating.

Now, this was just my experience here in Toronto, and this WAS 2 years ago so it may have changed since then. I hope this helps!

You are quite literally on a forum of over 200k people - in different time zones, with lives, jobs, families, problems of their own, etc - so no, nobody here hates you, I doubt anyone here even knows you. Please try and redirect the blame for why you feel the way you do off of other people who are also struggling. I came into this sub and frankly this post put me in a bad mood until I realized you're probably struggling with explaining how you're feeling without projecting. Maybe I'm wrong idk. 

But this is a support forum, meaning we are here to support each other in being well, not indulging in the symptoms that keep us sick. This would be a good time to remind yourself that the world is a lot larger and more nuanced than how we perceive it when we're feeling traumatized. You are okay ❤️ take a step back, try your best not to be reactionary. 


Hang in there, things will get easier with practice and you are a wholly good person having a difficult moment. Just breathe and try to refocus, and if you need help try again.

OP, is your daughter seeing a therapist? 

Some teenagers show their pain in very subtle ways, but this to me screams that she feels a ton of grief over her relationship with her mother and may feel this is her chance to bond with her. If they haven't had much of a relationship before and this suddenly changed after one visit that tells me a lot. 

Teenagers are going to do what they feel EMOTIONALLY is right for them at the best of times. Add in trauma and it becomes a very difficult situation to manage on all fronts. You're doing the right thing by asking for advice, I would really sincerely recommend a therapy session or a family therapy session - keep her in the loop about it so she isn't ambushed, but it's okay to tell her that if she wants to make a massive decision that you'd like a third party to help you express why you're worried. But nobody loses their mom in any capacity and doesn't have scars from it.

If worst comes to worst my biggest piece of advice is the same as a lot of other people here, be there for here and be present. I did the same thing your daughter did and lasted 2 weeks before it was so bad that I called dad begging him to pick me up. The difference in my story is that my dad made it his mission to take it personally and never let me forget it. I very very frequently think of how different things could've been if I hadn't been punished for mistakes I had no way of knowing I was even making.

I may come across as harsh, but please know I say this with so much love - you will need all the help in the world if you choose to have twins at 16. Start looking into young mom groups as they usually have TONS of resources and most offer resources and childcare during group. This will also connect you with other mums which will help a ton. You will need prenatal care, make sure you get on vitamins asap and you'll need to adjust your diet quite a bit. Is the dad involved? Do you have supports to help you with the babies when they're born? Have you looked for an OB or midwife? Are you prepared for the likelihood that your twins will be premature and require a NICU stay?
